Hut 8 brings exceptional people together to solve the world’s most consequential problems at the intersection of energy and technology. Today, that means building infrastructure for AI at a pace and scale without precedent. Tomorrow, it could mean powering a new era of innovation through robotics, advanced manufacturing, or an industry that does not yet exist. Whatever the technology demands, our ambition holds: to build the defining physical infrastructure company of our generation.

We look for thinkers and builders with the rigor, humility, and ownership to solve problems at this scale. They start from zero and choose truth over tradition. They back the best idea, whatever its source. They bet on themselves and embrace the hard truths that force them to grow. Our commitment is to keep the path from idea to execution short, trust them with critical decisions and the work that follows, and surround them with colleagues whose curiosity extends beyond their expertise.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Controls SME is Managed Services' controls and automation expert, embedded in a data center build. The role supports design review, vendor oversight, and commissioning to make sure the control systems are operable, maintainable, and trustworthy at turnover. Controls are the facility's nervous system: when they fail or mislead, operators lose sight of everything else.

Some of the key responsibilities you should expect are the following:

Operability Design Review
Review controls designs, including BMS/BAS, EPMS, SCADA, PLC-based plant controls, CDU and cooling plant controls, and generator, UPS, and switchgear controller integration, through an operations lens. Sequences of operations, failure-mode and fail-safe behavior, loss-of-network and loss-of-controller response, manual and local override, point lists and instrumentation adequacy, alarm philosophy and prioritization, graphics clarity, and OT network architecture and access control. Push back where the design assumes an operator will understand or recover something the system never tells them.


Controls QA/QC and Vendor Oversight
Provide QA/QC oversight of controls scope for new construction and retrofits: review vendor proposals and programming, directly oversee system configuration and component upgrades, and witness factory tests. Hold controls vendors to Hut 8 standards and to the approved sequences, and make sure every modification to a system follows change control.


Construction-Phase Verification
Walk controls installations at key milestones. Flag operability and quality issues to the MEP superintendent early, while they are still cheap to fix.


Commissioning
Witness Level 3-5 commissioning of controls and automation: point-to-point verification, sequence- of-operations testing, controller, server, and network failover, alarm verification, trend validation, and integrated systems testing across mechanical, electrical, and controls, including loss-of- communication and loss-of-BMS scenarios. Review programming through the commissioning process, drive operational findings into the Cx log with clear acceptance criteria, and verify closure personally.


Turnover Readiness
Verify controls turnover packages: as-built sequences of operation, point lists, control and network drawings, programming backups and configuration files under version control, licenses and credentials transferred to Hut 8, alarm setpoint and priority matrices, trend baselines, spare controllers and critical modules, and PM program inputs such as backup routines, firmware updates, and panel power health. Confirm the backups actually restore.


Training
Provide technical controls training and support to Facility Operations staff, and validate that operator training equips the team to use the systems, not just look at them.


Program Feedback
Feed operational lessons into Hut 8 controls standards, point naming and alarm conventions, and the next project's basis of design, and work with other Hut 8 sites and teams to carry standards across the portfolio.

ABOUT YOU
What we're looking for:

  • 7+ years of controls experience in programming, start-up, and commissioning of complex systems such as central plants, air handling units, and evaporative cooling and humidification systems. A bachelor's degree or trade certification in a related field plus 3+ years of controls industry experience will be considered in lieu.
  • Experience in critical environments, with a working knowledge of critical facility operations and procedure-based work.
  • Theoretical and practical understanding of control equipment and systems: design, maintenance, troubleshooting, testing, and construction.
  • Working knowledge of the mechanical, electrical, and life safety systems found in critical facilities.
  • Sequence-of-operations fluency: you can read one critically, catch the gaps and failure modes, and test whether it behaves as written.
  • Experience interpreting blueprints, CAD drawings, and controls diagrams.
  • Turnover documentation rigor, especially programming backups, configuration files, and version control.
  • Comfortable embedded with a construction team while holding the operations line, and effective in a highly collaborative, cross-functional environment.

Preferred:

  • Data center experience.
  • PLC programming experience
  • IT or networking certification
  • Equipment field service engineering or manufacturer representative experience.
  • Demonstrated use of AI tools to improve workflows with measurable results, such as efficiency gains or quality improvements.

ABOUT THE WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Full time on-site role.

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

  • Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

  • Analyze complex questions involving securities law, derivatives regulation, jurisdiction, and market structure.

  • Engage with the SEC, CFTC, and other regulatory bodies on registrations, product approvals, examinations, and regulatory inquiries.

  • Partner with Product, Markets, Compliance, and leadership to structure and launch new products within applicable regulatory frameworks.

  • Monitor regulatory developments and translate them into actionable recommendations for the business.

  • Work closely with internal and external counsel on regulatory strategy, enforcement matters, and other complex legal issues.

What We're Looking For

  • J.D. and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar.

  • 5 - 8+ years of relevant legal experience at a law firm, financial regulator, exchange, broker-dealer, or financial services company.

  • Deep understanding of SEC and/or CFTC regulatory frameworks, with demonstrated experience navigating issues involving securities, derivatives, or financial market structure.

  • Experience advising on complex regulatory matters involving financial products, trading platforms, or regulated market participants.

  • Exceptional legal research, writing, and analytical skills.

  • Strong commercial judgment and the ability to translate complex regulatory issues into practical business advice.

  • Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced environment with significant ambiguity.

Helpful Experience

Kalshi has minimal hierarchy and broad variance in experience levels within each title; if your compensation expectations exceed this range, we encourage you to reach out - we’re always happy to discuss.

Our Culture

Meritocracy is at our core, and we value people who take ownership and figure (usually hard) things out. We dream big. We love our craft deeply and are proud of what we put out in the world. We are committed to our vision of building something big… but also useful: a product that brings more truth through the power of markets.

Kalshians are Kalshi’s most important asset: we pick Kalshians carefully, so we trust them fully on day 1.

Commitment to Equal Opportunity

We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Specialist Solutions Architects (SSA) are domain experts aligned to specific Stripe solutions and customer buying centers. We have in-depth knowledge of specific solution offerings and a deep understanding of customer challenges. We align with specialist product sellers on deals, advise the broader pre-sales team on complex opportunities, support pipeline development and revenue attainment, serve as an advisor on go-to-market sales plays, and provide critical insights to our product and engineering teams.

Stripe Radar is Stripe's fully integrated fraud and risk management platform. The Radar team's mission is to evolve from a best-in-class payment fraud product into a unified risk intelligence platform that protects businesses from all forms of financial loss—from sophisticated payment fraud and account takeovers to first-party misuse and policy abuse. With Radar, businesses can confidently navigate the evolving fraud landscape, accept more good revenue, and focus on growth.

What you’ll do

You will collaborate closely with sales and pre-sales teams to drive pipeline and revenue targets, while also educating the product and engineering teams on market trends and strongly influencing the product roadmap. You will develop deep relationships with senior customer business leaders and grow Stripe's solution offerings with new and existing customers. As a subject matter expert, you will scale the broader organization by creating reusable assets and coaching others on complex, high-value opportunities. You will serve as the domain and product expert to our users and GTM team for Stripe Radar globally.

Responsibilities

  • Act as a subject matter expert on Stripe's Radar product suite to accelerate opportunities globally
  • Demonstrate a deep understanding of trends in the fraud and risk management ecosystem, including AI-powered detection, processor-agnostic architectures, and the shift from payment fraud to holistic business risk (policy abuse, account takeover, first-party misuse)
  • Develop expertise with the functional and architectural patterns for deploying advanced fraud systems, including the lifecycle of rule management, ML model tuning, and manual review optimization
  • Understand the ecosystem of risk and identity integrations (device fingerprinting, identity verification, bot mitigation, case management) Stripe must support for users to be successful
  • Define, share, and learn best practices and reusable assets with the broader GTM organization to enhance the quality and efficiency of the team
  • Create reference architectures to uplevel the team and refine reference solutions based on product enhancements and customer feedback
  • Partner closely with the Radar product sales team on Stripe's largest and most complex Radar opportunities, leading solution strategy and owning key customer relationships
  • Partner closely with the Radar product team to get early exposure to new products and features
  • Serve as a "Voice of the Customer" internally to drive product and feature request prioritization, providing actionable insights on the competitive landscape and emerging fraud vectors
  • Act as an escalation point to drive complex technical issues to resolution with Stripe's engineering team
  • Stay current on competitive analysis and market differentiation
  • Support marketing events including executive briefings, conferences, user groups, and trade shows

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

  • 7+ years of experience in a pre-sales, technical consulting, product, or risk strategy role focused on e-commerce fraud prevention, risk management, or trust and safety
  • Deep working knowledge of the fraud and risk ecosystem, including payment fraud (CNP), account takeover (ATO), first-party misuse (friendly fraud), and policy/content abuse
  • Demonstrated knowledge of risk management architectures, including the role of rules engines, machine learning models, and manual review queues in fraud decisioning
  • Strong knowledge of the signals and data used in fraud detection: device/IP data, behavioral biometrics, identity verification, and graph-based analysis
  • Strong knowledge of software engineering and architecture patterns, with the ability to understand how a wide variety of technologies and systems interact
  • Exceptional communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, comfortable explaining complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • A proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with business partners
  • Ability to deal effectively with ambiguity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-moving environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience integrating Stripe or other RESTful APIs into web applications
  • Experience with processor-agnostic fraud solutions and multi-processor payment environments
  • Experience with risk management for platforms/marketplaces, subscription services, and digital goods
  • Familiarity with liability shift programs (chargeback guarantees) and value-based pricing models for risk products
  • Understanding of how to extend fraud protection across the payment lifecycle—payouts (Issuing), in-person (Terminal), or recurring (Billing)
  • Experience as a subject matter expert in a relevant industry, vertical, or product

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

About the role

We are seeking a Technical Writer to own end-to-end developer documentation for Bitdeer AI's MaaS platform, spanning API reference, getting-started guides, and release notes for a fast-moving catalog of hosted chat, completion, embedding, and fine-tuning endpoints. Today, developers integrating against our inference API frequently have to reverse-engineer request and response shapes from internal Postman collections, ask engineering directly in Slack, or discover breaking parameter changes only after their integration fails in production, which slows time-to-first-successful-call and generates avoidable support load on the engineering team. This role fixes that by turning our OpenAPI specifications, model catalog, and endpoint behavior into accurate, versioned, always-current documentation that developers can trust as the single source of truth, and by establishing a release notes cadence that keeps pace with model and endpoint updates. The person who succeeds here is comfortable reading Go service code and API diffs well enough to write precisely about them, treats documentation as a product with its own release cycle rather than an afterthought, and can work independently across multiple engineering teams to pull accurate technical detail out of people who are not naturally inclined to write it down themselves.

What you will be responsible for:

  • API Reference Ownership: Maintain and continuously improve the OpenAPI-driven API reference covering chat/completions, embeddings, fine-tuning, and model routing endpoints. Verify that documented request/response schemas, error codes, and rate limits match actual service behavior by testing against staging and production endpoints. Work directly with backend engineers to capture new parameters, deprecations, and behavioral edge cases before they ship to customers.
  • Getting-Started and Onboarding Guides: Design and maintain the guides that take a new developer from signing up to making their first successful inference call, including authentication, SDK quickstarts, and common integration patterns across supported languages. Continuously identify drop-off points in the onboarding funnel through support tickets and developer feedback, and rewrite the weakest steps first. Keep sample code runnable and tested against the live API rather than left to go stale.
  • Release Notes and Changelog Discipline: Establish and run a recurring release notes process tied to model catalog updates, new endpoints, pricing changes, and breaking API changes, so developers are never surprised by a change in production. Coordinate with product and engineering release cadences to publish notes before or at the moment of rollout, and clearly flag deprecations, migration steps, and timelines for removal.
  • Docs-as-Code Pipeline and Information Architecture: Own the documentation toolchain (Markdown/MDX, Git-based review, OpenAPI spec linting and generation) so that docs are versioned, reviewable, and testable the same way code is. Organize the growing surface area of models, endpoints, and guides into an information architecture that stays navigable as the model catalog expands. Reduce duplicated or contradictory content across reference, guides, and internal wikis.
  • Cross-functional Technical Fact-Finding: Interview engineers, PMs, and support staff to extract accurate technical detail on new features, model behavior quirks, and known limitations, and turn ad hoc knowledge into structured, discoverable documentation. Sit in on model launch and API design reviews early enough to document decisions and rationale, not just final syntax, and push back when proposed APIs or error messages would be confusing to document or to use.
  • Developer Feedback Loop: Instrument and monitor documentation usage signals (search queries with no results, support tickets referencing missing or wrong docs, doc page feedback) to prioritize what to fix next. Report recurring documentation gaps back to engineering and product as a proxy for API usability issues, not just writing quality issues.

  • Have working familiarity with a docs-as-code toolchain: Markdown/MDX, Git-based version control and pull request review, and static site generators or documentation platforms (e.g., Docusaurus, Mintlify, ReadMe, GitBook, or equivalent).
